themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal complaints spiked to 4 reports this week compared to 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting a possible infrastructure failure or outage affecting traffic flow in Flatlands/Canarsie this week.
evidence: 4 traffic signal complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
967% spike with z-score of 7.49 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Traffic signal condition is among top 10 complaint categories district-wide (402 complaints in 90 days)
reporting_angles: Are multiple signals down simultaneously in a specific corridor, or is this a scattered pattern? Check DOT maintenance logs.
Interview DOT and residents on whether this is causing safety issues, accidents, or gridlock during peak hours.

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 28 reports this week versus 7.9 per week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 256% spike (z-score: 7.18)—suggesting a new noisy business, event, or construction activity emerged in the district this week.
evidence: 28 commercial noise complaints this week vs. 7.9 weekly average (256% increase)
Z-score of 7.18 indicates statistically significant deviation from baseline
Residential noise is also a top complaint category (1,014 over 90 days), suggesting noise is a district-wide issue
reporting_angles: Investigate which business, construction project, or venue is generating the spike. Cross-reference with DOB permits filed in the past 2 weeks.
Interview affected residents in neighborhoods closest to complaint hotspots; determine if NYPD or 311 enforcement actions have been taken.

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 8 reports this week versus 1.0 per week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 7.0)—indicating a new or non-compliant cannabis business, or enforcement crackdown, emerged this week in Flatlands/Canarsie.
evidence: 8 cannabis retailer complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
Z-score of 7.0 indicates highly significant statistical anomaly
This is a nascent issue in the district—minimal baseline suggests this is genuinely new activity this week
reporting_angles: Has a new unlicensed cannabis shop opened, or did an existing one expand operations? Check with NYC's Office of Cannabis Management for recent licenses issued in CD 318.
Interview residents about specific complaints: odor, loitering, illegal sales, or operation outside licensed hours. Determine if CB or elected officials have been notified.

themes_detail.label: Street and Sidewalk Deterioration Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, street condition complaints nearly tripled (52 this week vs. 20.1 weekly average, +158%), root/sewer/sidewalk complaints more than tripled (8 this week vs. 2.6 average, +205%), and overgrown tree/branch complaints quadrupled (13 this week vs. 3.1 average, +316%), suggesting concentrated infrastructure neglect or recent storm damage in one or more neighborhoods.
evidence: Street condition: 52 complaints this week vs. 20.1 weekly average (+158%, z-score: 4.63)
Root/sewer/sidewalk condition: 8 complaints this week vs. 2.6 weekly average (+205%, z-score: 5.42)
Overgrown tree/branches: 13 complaints this week vs. 3.1 weekly average (+316%, z-score: 4.27)
Together, these three categories represent 73 complaints in a single week—more than 2.5× normal load
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm, freeze-thaw cycle, or flooding event that destabilized streets and uprooted trees? Cross-reference with weather data.
Map the complaints geographically: are they concentrated in specific neighborhoods or spread across the district? This reveals whether it's a localized vs. systemic problem.
Interview Parks Dept. and NYC Department of Environmental Protection on maintenance backlogs and timeline for repairs.

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk/Dangling Sign Infrastructure Issues
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints tripled to 3 this week versus 1.0 per week average (200% increase, z-score: 4.0), and damaged tree complaints are elevated at 15 last week versus 6.1 weekly average (+145%), indicating potential weather damage or deferred maintenance affecting public infrastructure this week.
evidence: Dangling street signs: 3 complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (200% increase, z-score: 4.0)
Damaged trees: 15 complaints last week vs. 6.1 weekly average (+145%, z-score: 4.03)
These are part of a broader infrastructure cluster affecting streets, trees, and sidewalks this week
reporting_angles: Was there recent severe weather (wind, ice) that loosened signs and damaged tree limbs? Cross-check with NWS and Parks Dept. reports.
Are dangling signs a safety hazard? Visit locations with complaints and photograph; interview residents on risk perception.
